segments.text: Good afternoon. I reserved a quiet room for two nights under the name Laura Green.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: I found your reservation, Ms. Green. The quiet room won't be ready until six, but a room near the elevator is available now.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: I'd rather wait. Can I leave my suitcase here while I get something to eat?

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Certainly. We'll keep it behind the front desk and call you when your room is ready.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Question. What does the man say about the quiet room?

items.prompt:
Synthesize the exact two-person dialogue below as audio for an English listening examination.
Do not speak these instructions, the speaker labels, or the transcript boundary labels.
Woman is one adult woman and must always use the assigned Woman voice.
Man is one adult man and must always use the assigned Man voice.
Every Woman-labeled line must use only the same Woman voice.
Every Man-labeled line must use only the same Man voice.
Never merge, substitute, swap, imitate, or transfer the two voices.
Never let either speaker read a line assigned to the other speaker.
The difference between the adult woman and adult man must remain clearly audible in every turn.
Use natural American English suitable for Japanese high school learners.
Use a gently unhurried conversational pace, a little slower than ordinary conversation but not noticeably slow.
Maintain a steady pace.
Do not rush, accelerate, over-enunciate, or stretch individual words.
After the Number line, pause clearly for about 0.80 seconds.
At each change between Woman and Man, use a brief natural pause of about 0.55 seconds.
After saying "Question," pause clearly for about 0.60 seconds before reading the question text.
Do not add other deliberate pauses.
Use natural intonation without sounding theatrical or robotic.
Do not emphasize any detail in a way that reveals the answer.
Read every transcript word exactly once. Do not add, omit, repeat, paraphrase, or explain anything.

Woman: Number 2.
Woman: Good afternoon. I reserved a quiet room for two nights under the name Laura Green.
Man: I found your reservation, Ms. Green. The quiet room won't be ready until six, but a room near the elevator is available now.
Woman: I'd rather wait. Can I leave my suitcase here while I get something to eat?
Man: Certainly. We'll keep it behind the front desk and call you when your room is ready.
Woman: Question. What does the man say about the quiet room?
END TRANSCRIPT
